## Role and Cost Boundary

This page owns marine and terrestrial installation of infield and export cables: mobilisation, route preparation, laying, burial or trenching, protection, pull-ins, installation jointing, testing and reinstatement. Cable manufacture is costed on the relevant cable page.

| Physical scope | Treatment | Cost owner |
|---|---|---|
| Cable manufacture and supply accessories | Excluded | [Infield AC Cables](../electrical_infra/infield_ac_cables.qmd) or [HVDC Export Cables](../electrical_infra/hvdc_export_cables.qmd) |
| Route preparation and clearance | Included here | **This page** |
| Marine laying and burial | Included here | **This page** |
| Landfall, trenching, ducts and reinstatement | Included here | **This page** |
| Pull-ins, installation joints and testing | Included here | **This page** |
| Major crossings, tunnels and exceptional protection | Included here when specified separately | **This page** |

<span class="cost-owned">Green = booked on this page</span>
<span class="cost-reference">Grey = reference only; not booked on this page</span>

## Export-Cable Installation Reference

The NREL Atlantic Offshore Wind Transmission Study separates material and installation for a 525 kV, 2 GW HVDC bipole [@brinkman2024AtlanticTransmission]. The values below use the ECB 2025 annual-average exchange rate of 1 EUR = 1.1300 USD [@ecb2025USDEUR].

| NREL component | Converted route cost | Cost owner |
|---|---:|---|
| Cable material | <span class="cost-reference">EUR 2.51 million/km</span> | [HVDC Export Cables](../electrical_infra/hvdc_export_cables.qmd) |
| Cable installation | <span class="cost-owned">EUR 1.48 million/km</span> | **This page** |
| Material + installation | <span class="cost-reference">EUR 4.00 million/km</span> | Shared perspective only |

The conversion changes currency only. The NREL price year, route conditions, landfall scope and compatibility with TenneT's dedicated metallic-return design must still be confirmed before using it as a constant-2026-euro model input.

::: {.callout-important}
## Significant installation cost favours higher-capacity assets

In the NREL reference, installation is about EUR 1.48 million/km compared with EUR 2.51 million/km for cable material. Much of the installation cost is driven by the route, mobilisation, vessel campaign, burial, crossings and pull-ins rather than increasing directly with transmitted capacity. This creates an economic tendency to use higher-capacity cables—and similarly higher-capacity [pipelines](pipeline_installation.qmd)—because the route-installation cost is spread over more transported power or product.

That tendency is not unlimited. Cable mass, handling limits, manufacturing availability, electrical losses, redundancy requirements and the consequence of losing one large asset can favour multiple smaller systems.
:::

## Installed-System Cross-Checks

### Adriatic Link

Prysmian's 2023 Adriatic Link award is approximately EUR 630 million for design, supply, installation and commissioning of a 1 GW bipolar link with about 210 km subsea and 40 km underground route [@prysmian2023AdriaticLink]. This is EUR 2.52 million/km across the mixed route.

Applying the DEA underground-to-subsea cost ratio and the report's 2023-to-2026 restatement factor gives an inferred 2026 subsea rate of EUR 2.60 million/km.

This remains a **complete installed-system** inference. The contract does not disclose its material/installation split.

### Danish Energy Agency

The DEA gives 2025 planning values at the 2020 price level for a 1.5--2 GW DC cable system [@danishEnergyAgency2025Transport]. At 2 GW and restated to 2026 euros, they give:

| DEA EPC route | 2026-euro reference | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| Subsea DC cable system | <span class="cost-reference">EUR 8.14 million/km</span> | Equipment plus installation/EPC context at 2 GW |
| Underground DC cable system | <span class="cost-reference">EUR 10.28 million/km</span> | Equipment plus installation/EPC context at 2 GW |

These are not installation-only values.

## Existing Internal Assumptions

| Installation item | Route cost | Interpretation | Status | Cost owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Infield cable installation | <span class="cost-owned">EUR 635,000 per laid cable-km</span> | Individual array-cable route | Current internal assumption | **This page** |
| Export cable installation | <span class="cost-reference">EUR 635,000 per system route-km</span> | Complete-system scope is unresolved | Not adopted | **This page** |
| NREL export installation | <span class="cost-owned">EUR 1.48 million per system route-km</span> | Complete 525 kV, 2 GW bipole reference | Provisional replacement reference | **This page** |

The identical EUR 635,000/km assumptions for an individual infield cable and a complete HVDC system do not demonstrate equal physical installation cost. The export value remains excluded from the model until its scope is reconciled.

The installer benchmark for Vanguard East and West records about EUR 600 million of installation-related cost for 452 km of infield cabling, approximately EUR 1.3 million/km [@installerInfieldCableBenchmark]. It is an upper contextual comparison because its package scope may include mobilisation, pull-ins, jointing and project overheads.

## Installation Sequence

The route-specific model should cover:

1. surveys, clearance and pre-lay grapnel runs;
2. cable load-out and transport;
3. marine laying and simultaneous or post-lay burial;
4. crossings and external protection;
5. offshore pull-in and termination support;
6. landfall, trenching or directional drilling;
7. terrestrial installation and reinstatement; and
8. testing and as-laid/as-buried survey.

## Bottom-Up Cost Model

$$
C_\mathrm{cable\ installation}
=
C_\mathrm{mobilisation}
+\sum_v r_vt_v
+C_\mathrm{landfall}
+C_\mathrm{crossings}
+C_\mathrm{civil}
+C_\mathrm{testing}.
$$

The model must distinguish individual cable-kilometres from system route-kilometres and account for separate pole, return and communication cables where applicable.

## Principal Cost Drivers

| Driver | Effect |
|---|---|
| Number and mass of physical cables | Controls campaigns, load-outs and vessel capacity |
| Burial depth and soil | Controls tool selection and production rate |
| Crossings and rock placement | Add materials, vessels and schedule |
| Landfall method | Open cut, trenching and directional drilling have different cost structures |
| Weather and vessel availability | Affect waiting time and mobilisation risk |
| Jointing strategy | Controls offshore or onshore jointing time and repair compatibility |

## Model Limitations

| Limitation | Implication |
|---|---|
| NREL source price year is unresolved | The euro conversion is not yet a constant-2026-euro input |
| Installed benchmarks bundle material and installation | They are validation points, not installation coefficients |
| Existing export EUR 635,000/km scope is unresolved | It is not used as the adopted HVDC installation cost |
| Route and vessel schedule are not yet parameterised | Site-specific installation cost remains unavailable |
